utterances.text: Provide the Prosecution and the Bench with copies and --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do that straight away, Mr. President, yes. The number is D13, a first exhibit. Can I hand it over to the registrar -- the usher, I'm sorry. To the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, would you please collect the ... Yes, and please distribute them. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't think the witness has received a copy of the text yet. Could the witness be given it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just before that takes place, I have now found the passage which my friend read out about ten minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Which he read out as follows: They were terribly stressed along the front lines, so you didn't see many of them in the city.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please indicate also what page it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes. Page 1320.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Commencing at line 5, and it reads, in English --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: "The forces were so thin that they were terribly, terribly stretched, out along the front lines, so you didn't see much of them in the city." So it appears that the witness's recollection was in fact correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is correct. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I'm positively sorry. What I have is "stressed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It might be that you have the provisional copy and that they have later been corrected. So this is a misunderstanding. I can't blame anyone for.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I go ahead with my question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: First question, sir: Do you speak French?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who are you asking? Are you asking me that question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. No, not -- no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why did you state in your written statement that you spoke French?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I studied French. I can understand a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why have you just told me that you don't speak French?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I'm not fluent. I don't speak it every day. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. The photograph that you have in front of you, what type of weapon, with technical details, does this represent? And when I say a technical definition of the weapon, what I mean is, is it a T-57, 58, 54, or whatever. Give us the numbers that the weapon is identified by.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This looks like a modified T-55 or possibly a T-64. It has a 100-millimetre gun on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So you think it is a T-55 or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It looks like a modified T-55, or possibly a T-64.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: And now I'd like to present another document. We're going to produce it, under the following number: D13. And I'd like to tender it to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The document just given to us bears the number D13, so there might be -- if you're talking about another document --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, we're talking about D14. I apologise. Thank you very much. Can I hand it to the usher? And I'm going to ask the witness the same question for each of these documents, each of the following documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The same question for you, witness.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We have D17 and D18. Just a moment, please. We also have D19, D20, and D21 is the last one. utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the Bench be provided with the -- until D15 has been distributed. Yes? Okay. Mr. Ashton, you may answer the same question in respect of photographs D15.

utterances.text: Oh, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.text: Yes. Could you please put them on the ELMO. We're having them put on the ELMO. Thank you, Madam Registrar. So D16, the question has been answered. Could you please now put on the ELMO the picture D17.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] D18.

utterances.text: Yes. You may --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with the earlier Soviet-style tank, but this looks like to a T-32, T-34, in that this is a much older version than the T-54, T-55. It's the previous version. It could be Yugoslav version. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's 30 or 40?

utterances.text: You've stated 32?

utterances.text: Thank you. D19, please. I'm sorry. D18?

utterances.text: I think the question --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. D19.

utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies. D19, please.

utterances.text: Hold on just a minute. I need to look at this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Take your time. Take your time. Excuse me.

utterances.text: This has been -- this is slightly modified. We're going back to D18, please, Exhibit D18.

utterances.text: Please do. I believe you still have it in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This looks more consistent with the T-54, prior to conversion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So this one is therefore a tank you refer to, that is the tank that you refer to when you told us you had seen a position somewhere around Sarajevo. I'm referring to the map that you annotated, that you yourself annotated.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not the tank I saw there, no. It doesn't -- the image coming up on D20 is the one that looks more similar to the tank that I saw at the ...

utterances.text: But you have just stated, sir, that it was a T-54?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The model T-54 that you saw on location which is mentioned in the map that you yourself annotated, was it a T-54 not-modified model?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]

utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think we were discussing D19, Mr. President. Am I right?

utterances.text: D20, please?
