utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: The models that we see on D18 and D19 -- no. Sorry. D19 and D20, are they consistent with the types of tanks that you saw and indicated on the map that you annotated?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: D20 definitely, yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it from the side, so yes, I can identify D20 for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So D21 would be the same, that is, the same question concerning D21, please?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Also a T-54 that we talked with?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: T-54, T-55 version, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Mr. Ashton, and I will finish with this topic. I have a couple of more questions to ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm referring to line 18:04:33 and the following line in my transcript, that is, the transcript of January 9th, 2002, in particular, line 18:04:56.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... because I have the final transcript from the 9th of January, which does not indicate any times. So we have to find it. Could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm very sorry, Mr. President, but since I work abroad during the weekend, I don't always have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... sort this out. Could you please give the line, at least quote what it is so that we can try to find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have any other reference, but the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... please quote it so that we can find it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The text is as follows: You were talking about the tank that you had seen above Grbavica. You testified as follows: [In English] "The third I actually saw. The tank withdrew after the shooting." [Interpretation] Do you confirm this, sir: If the tank had withdrawn -- I'm sorry, the exact quote is withdrew - it means that you actually saw it withdraw?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I saw the tank reverse.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: My question, consequently, is as follows: Why didn't you take any photos of this tank since it seems that you had come to that area in order to take photographs?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I can now indicate where that passage is in the revised transcript. It appears on page 1245.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: At line 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your assistance, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Concerning the interpretation, it's not that it appears or it seems; it is that the witness had actually said that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Why didn't you take any photographs, since you were able to see the tank and you had actually come to that location in order to take photographs?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That image was -- I was in the window of the Holiday Inn when this incident occurred, and I had run out of film. I had taken several rolls of film. There was a CBS camera crew, so I was watching through my lens and pointing out to them where the tank was. I was waiting for another photographer to come in to loan me some film, but by then, when she arrived, it was too dark.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So are you saying that it was much too dark to see?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was early -- about 4.00 in the afternoon when the tank came out, but I was there for almost three and a half, four hours. I have images that where the shells were landing and I couldn't find the tank for quite some time and eventually it came out in the clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few more questions and I will be finishing my part of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, am I correct if I say that you have testified before this Chamber that you heard talks about a price consisting of 300 German marks, concerning foreign journalists who were targeted or hit by snipers? I have not used the term "foreign journalists" just "journalist," in respect of each journalist. Is it correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Have you ever heard General Galic issue an order concerning such a price to be given in this sense?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you ever heard any officers under the authority of General Galic issue such an order?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you ever heard, sir, General Galic issue any execution order to any officer?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Apologies of the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Concerning an iron cross, at any point in time.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Have you ever heard, sir, any of the officers under the authority of General Galic issue any execution order concerning the so-called fire cross --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Iron cross, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, have you ever seen, because you could have seen and not only heard, any officer under the authority of General Galic issue any such order -- any such orders? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In reference to this iron cross pattern?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I said orders, in plural, not only in respect of iron cross but also in respect of prices in cases of attacks on journalists. I was referring to the price?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, okay. That's different. No, I did not hear of any officer say that there was an order or given an order to shoot journalists for a price. No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions for the witness. This concludes my cross-examination of the witness, and my colleague will continue with the cross-examinations, as we previously agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... one final question at this moment. The question put to you, Mr. Ashton, by Mr. Piletta-Zanin whether you heard any officer to give any of such orders or that you have seen such orders to be given, the last part of the question has not been answered yet.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in reference to the killing of the journalist or the "iron cross."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Ashton. Ms. Pilipovic, you then may proceed in the cross-examination of Mr. Ashton.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ashton, let me say hello, and I shall be asking you questions from now on. First of all, I would like you to confirm that to the investigators of the Prosecution you gave three statements. The first statement was dated the 25th, 26th, and 27th of June, 1995; the second statement is dated the 29th and 31st of October and 1st of November, 2001; and the third statement was dated the 12th to the 14th of November, 2001. Is that correct? Did you give those statements and did you sign them?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Together with the statement that you gave to the investigator on the 12th, 13th, and 14th of November, and the 29th, 30th, and 31st of October, 2001, and the 1st of November, 2001, you also provided an annex concerning the explanation of photographs that you handed over to the Prosecution. And according to your words, you took those photographs during your stay in Sarajevo. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise, on the 1st of November, 2001, together with the statement which is dated October and up until the 1st of November, 2001, you also included some positions that you annotated according to your recollection, and you indicated those positions on the map that you signed on the 1st of November, 2001, the map which you provided to the Prosecution and which was subsequently provided to the Defence by the Prosecution; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir, that the dates contained in your statements correspond exactly to the incidents which took place during your stay in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some dates correspond exactly, some are within a couple of weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to that question, for this reason: That the question invites the witness to confirm, indeed to agree with the Defence, that the dates in the statements, that's plural, correspond to the incidents. The first paragraph in the last of those three statements carries a qualification by the witness to the effect that he at that point has available his journals and that his notes and correspondence, and as a result, in that statement, he's able to give a fuller account, and I quote these words "with any appropriate additions or alterations." Therefore, the question in its phrasing could not embrace the dates of the three statements where there are some alterations and inconsistencies. So that extent, it tends to mislead the witness, and I think it's important that Your Honours are aware of that situation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is sustained. If the first lines just quoted by Mr. Ierace are correct in the third statement. If not, please tell the Court, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I do not agree with the objection raised by my learned colleague from the Prosecution, because the intention of the Defence was to ask a question concerning each statement, in particular, the statement given on the 12th and the 14th of November, and that is the reason why we wanted to know whether all of those statements were given by the witness and signed by the witness. So my question following that would be as follows: Which of these three statements is more accurate? Since the witness told us that there was some approximation in his dates. And I just wanted to have the witness confirm that the statement that he gave on the 12th and 14th of November was as follows, "not in any one such case was I able to use my notes or correspondence from the times of the events that I am describing and that I'm referring to as my journal. Now I've had the opportunity to review my documents and provide more details." The Defence wanted to have the witness confirm that it is in this statement that the dates are probably more accurate, and I would follow that with further questions, in view of the fact that the witness referred to his journal. I think that the objection of my learned colleague was somewhat premature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think it related to your first question, which made no distinction between any of these statements, and I wonder whether the objection is also valid for the question indicated by Ms. Pilipovic. She would like to put to the witness as a second question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I have no difficulty with the second question, Mr. President, but my friend just purported to read out the paragraph, the first paragraph in the last of the three statements. I am concerned that perhaps she does not have an accurate translation, because --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is the interpreters who were not provided with the appropriate reference, so what you received was just a simultaneous interpretation of the words of the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The passage which my friend quoted contained this as the last sentence. This is the last sentence of the first paragraph in the third statement of the witness: "Now I've had the opportunity to review my documents and provide more details." In fact, in the original English version, that last sentence reads: "I have now been able to go through my records and give a fuller account with any appropriate additions or alterations, to the best of my recollection." If my friend does not have that in B/C/S, then she needs to understand that's what the witness said in his last statement. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber noticed the difference in you quotation and the quotation of Ms. Pilipovic. Ms. Pilipovic, there is a difference in the lines quoted by Mr. Ierace and your reference to these lines. Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, with Your Honour's indulgence, I should like to intervene. The text that I have in front of me was correctly quoted in Serbian by Ms. Pilipovic, and there was -- there is a difference in the text, the text that was quoted in English and the Serbian text. So I'm sure we will once again have a problem with translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please, over one of the breaks to come, verify with the original text spoken -- no, the original text in the statement, because that's what we are talking about. I assume that there have been recordings of these statements as well, Mr. Ierace. Am I correct? I mean, this is not the place and the time to solve this problem, because we have to investigate it, at least the parties have to investigate why there are two different versions of these first lines, and this Chamber would be -- would welcome your explanation as soon as you have discussed the matter and as soon as you have found out. Ms. Pilipovic, since the second question you intended to put to the witness, there is no problem, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Let me just indicate that I do have the original in front of me, the English translation. The document that I received from the Prosecution, 03041593, I do not wish to be misunderstood. I am not misinterpreting anything that is contained in this statement. It is my objective to establish the truth in this case. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that in the statement that you gave on the 12th and the 14th of November, the portion of which I have just read out to you, you were not able to use -- to refer to your notes which you made at the time of the events and that you had now been able -- been given this opportunity. Would you tell us something more about the way that you kept your notes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I object to the question. The question presumes to reflect the evidence given by the witness, and to that end, it says that the witness did not have his notes available to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the time of the statements given.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That's clear. I think this must be a mistake by Ms. Pilipovic. You may proceed. It's common understanding, I think, in this courtroom that it was the time of giving the statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. In the statement which the witness gave on the 12th and the 14th of November, the witness stated, "I have now been able to go through my records." And my question concerned the way in which he kept his notes. When I say "the way," I'm referring both to the way he kept his records technically and to the time framework.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You may answer the question, Mr. Ashton.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every day, in the evening, I would sit down and I would write down a lengthy four, five, six, ten pages, however many required, to describe the day's events. I would occasionally draw a diagram or a map of something I wanted to explain that was complex. I kept notes of things that I saw individually which were not put into the relevant journal but were in a notebook, reporter's notebook. And each day I would conclude this before I went to bed, and then I would do it again the next day. Certain days when there was heavy shelling and I couldn't go out in the street, I would sit and write about events. When I was in the hospital, I would write about events in detail right after the surgeries were finished. In the event that I took a picture, I wrote a caption to send with the picture back to New York, with specifics. Does that answer the question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: May I take it, then, that you wrote every evening when you were able to do so, that you would, in the evening, write out, in your own handwriting, the things you had observed during the day, you would make a note of them in the evening in your own handwriting?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you wrote this out by hand, in your own handwriting? That's right, is it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some was in handwriting, some was on a computer at a later time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, the one you gave to the investigators of the Prosecution on the 29th and 30th of October and the 1st of November, on page 4 of that statement, of the B/C/S version, you stated the following: "When I say diary, I mean all notes and letters on a laptop computer and not a diary as in notebook form." Could you tell me what is correct: Was the diary your laptop computer version or do you mean by "diary" what you actually wrote down in a notebook?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until September, when I returned from Germany, I was writing handwritten journals in a notebook, after which, when I was working for UNHCR, I was able to write on a computer. Annotations and general notes were taken in a notebook that incidents or little details.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As I understood you to say that most of your observations which you took down were taken down on a laptop computer, over a longer period of time, because you said, actually, that it was just until you returned from Germany that you wrote them down in hand, in handwriting. Can we then agree that most of your journal was memorised, if I can put it that way, in the laptop computer? I said "journal" because you said that under "journal" you mean all the notes and letters you kept on the laptop computer.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you cannot, because you refer here to I said journal because you said that under journal you meant, and I quote, unquote, "notes and letters you kept on a laptop computer." No. I wrote notes, I wrote letters to people, in handwriting. I executed a journal in handwriting for the first several months until September, at which time I wrote from then on on a computer, but I still did some handwritten notes as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to clarify the matter of your journal. When I -- when you said "journal," you say to refer to my notes and correspondence which I kept on my laptop." So when you say "journal," you mean the notes and correspondence kept on your laptop computer; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's partially correct, it's partially wrong. I'm also referring to the journals, handwritten journals that I kept when I first arrived in Sarajevo through the time that I returned in September, as well as what I put on the computer later on, a journal being information that I recorded, whether by hand or by computer, it's a journal of my daily events, what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Most of your observations during your stay in Sarajevo were noted where? In the laptop computer or the journal in the notebook?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Much of it was in -- let me see if I can understand your question correctly here. My observations were equal and both. I had extensive writing in the journals. I had more time to write, so I had a lot more detail in the beginning, as I was doing medical work there, I had less time to write, and the computer journal was not as extensive, I would say, as the earlier journals written by hand.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1995, when you gave your statement to the investigators of the Tribunal, you said that you did not have access to all portions of the journal that you kept during your stay in Bosnia, and six years later you told the investigators the following: That you now do possess your notes. Could you tell us the reason why you were not able, for six years, to come into possession of the notes you kept, both in the laptop and in the notebook? Why was this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you are saying that for six years the witness was not able to come into the possession of the notes he kept. As far as I understand is that you refer to his first statement six years ago, that he had not available to him these notes or not full notes available to him, and that six years later he said that he had them available to him. I did not hear the witness say that it took him six years to collect his notes. Could you please either indicate a source for not having been able for six years to recover his notes, or rephrase your question, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the witness statement dated the 12th to the 14th of November, that is to say, none of those cases when statements were given, I was not able to use my notes and correspondence or letters. That's what the witness says in that statement. And my question is that if we look at the date that the first statement was given and in October, he said that in none of those cases was he able to use his notes, miscellaneous notes. I can rephrase the question and ask him the following.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Why, what was the reason that in this case, in 1995, and in October 2001 he was not able to use his notes?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to the question that you're asking, Ms. Pilipovic, is the fact that I did have access to many of the notes all along, which I've provided prior to that date. However, there were other notes that I had sent to the United States. I had sent to other friends, copies, and I had access to those only later on. I had to track people down and get some help to recover them. The notes have always been available.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you in possession of those notes today?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When I mean "now," I don't mean here in the courtroom, when I say "today," I don't mean in the courtroom, but at home. Do you have the originals at home?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am, I do have.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May we agree that the statement you made on the 12th and 14th of November, 2001, in view of the fact that you used your journal and your notes, is the most precise version with respect to date and with respect to your recollections of the time that you were in Sarajevo, if we compare it to the statement made a month before and the statement made in 1995?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Specific reference to certain dates of certain particular events, yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that you arrived in Sarajevo on the 5th of July, 1992, for two days, for a two-day stay. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My arrival was actually on the 6th, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, let's accept that it was the 6th, then, the 6th of July, 1992. How frequently before that 6th of July, 1992, did you travel to Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had never been before that date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far were you acquainted with the town of Sarajevo and its environs when you arrived on that 6th of July? How well did you know it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I knew very little other than what I had seen in media coverage of the Olympics, which did not cover the city of Sarajevo itself but the surroundings, and I was briefed by UNHCR in Zagreb, and I did a little reading, but I really had no detailed knowledge of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In the statement you made on the 12th and 14th of November, you said that from the 5th of July, and I'm quoting page 2 of that statement of yours, "From the 5th of July to the 27th of September, 1992, I was an independent photographer engaged by myself, but I sent the films to Time Magazine."

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think that should be the 28th of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please check that, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said the 28th of September. From the 5th of July, to the 28th of September, 2000. Perhaps the interpreters didn't hear me, but I'm reading from the statement in B/C/S. So from the 5th of July to the 28th of September, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that in the space of two days, you received papers, you were accredited as a freelance photographer, self-employed freelance photographic journalist. Now, who allowed you to make films in Sarajevo who gave you the papers to do so?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't state in two days what -- at least, if I did, it would have been in Zagreb prior to coming to Sarajevo. What I did was come to Zagreb first. It was there I was briefed by UNHCR and sent to UNPROFOR to get my credentials. I did have a registered business called International Images in New York city. It's a photo agency that belonged to me, and I applied for my credentials under my images. I provided my New York press credentials, my New York city police credentials, and I was given the UNPROFOR press credentials, as was routine for all journalists coming in and out of Bosnia or Croatia to work with the UN system.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I've just had pointed out to me that the transcript, at line 14:12:13:34 refers to my New York city police credentials. That should be press credentials.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correction. I did state police credentials.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I withdraw that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Up until the 28th of September, that means you were an independent photojournalist, self-employed freelance photojournalist, as you say, a self-employed freelance journalist, photojournalist, and that you sent your films to Time magazine; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. I was an employee of my company.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it also correct that you sent your films to Time magazine?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that throughout your stay in Sarajevo, you had your Nikon camera with you all the time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had my Nikon camera with me in Sarajevo the entire time I was there, in and out, but I did not have it with me at all times. There were certain areas I went to that I was afraid to take it to.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Will you tell us what places you visited where you weren't allowed to take your camera with you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told specifically by Colonel Indic not to bring a camera into his area and photograph anything except passing in and out through the -- to Central Bosnia. That was acceptable, but not to photograph any military events.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did you meet Colonel Indic for the first time? Where and when, actually?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first time I met him at Sarajevo airport, in September.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what year and could you give us a closer date for September?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry. It was September 1992. It was somewhere in the week of the 15th, in that area, September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand, up until the 15th of September, until you had met Colonel Indic, you always had your camera with you. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You have also said that in the Presidency, you went to the Presidency every day and that it was generally early in the morning, at around 8.00. Is it correct when you say that it was every day? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not every day. There was a press conference in the mornings there for journalists, and I occasionally did not go.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't always go. And when you went to the UNPROFOR building, I understand that it was in the PTT building. Who did you contact in the PTT building concerning UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, Fabrizio Hothchild, who was the UNHCR officer there, who was the UNHCR representative, but I had other contacts in UNHCR too that I contacted, and also World Food Programme and other UN agencies working there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that on the -- you remained until -- in the Holiday Inn until the 28th of September. I accept the fact that from the 2nd of August to the 22nd of August you were not in Sarajevo but you were undergoing treatment. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 2nd of August is when I left Sarajevo; that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did you return? You said you returned on the 22nd of August?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your statement, in all three statements, the first, second, and third, you explained an incident that took place on the 14th of July, when you were crossing the street from the Holiday Inn. Do you remember the incident I'm talking about?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In your first statement, the one you gave in 1995, you said that sniper fire was opened on an old woman and a girl. That is on page 2 of your statement in the B/C/S version and it is paragraph 5, line 3. And you said that she was being fired on from across the river towards Mount Trebevic. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to have the witness shown a map, the map which my learned colleagues gave to the witness and the witness used. It is number 3644, in which he drew in the positions when asked by my learned friend to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this 3644 or 3645, as I have Prosecution Exhibit -- not -- it's still a document, not yet tendered in evidence. 3645, that's the marked map. Is that the map you mean?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it is 3644, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Did you mean 3644.AA?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 44, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That's right, yes. It is the map that we decided would be shown to every witness, and I think that this present witness marked some positions on that particular map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I should like to ask the camera to zoom in on the part that you were marking so that we can have a better view. Will you indicate the street the incident took place on. Let's decide what marker pen, what colour marker pen we're going to use to mark this in for Defence, in response to Defence questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Black was what I saw that the witness used on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Very well. Thank you. I don't know whether black would be visible enough, because the map is black. Perhaps another colour would be better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but we had a general decision that black would be the colour of the Defence while red would be the colour of the ... so it becomes unclear, we'll see how to solve it, but let's start with black.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On the map, draw in -- mark in the street where the incident took place, please.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This street here that I just marked. Should I put a number there for you?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and could you tell me what street that is, the name of the street, if you know it? If not, never mind?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First put the number in it. I don't know what number we were at at this map, but black "1" would do, because I think it's the first black marking on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To avoid confusion, I was going to suggest if Your Honour might, D1 for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, or A, B, C. I don't know whether there are any letters on it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So that's marked D1 now. Yes. I think the next question was the name of the street, Mr. Ashton.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zmaja Od Bosna, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know the name of the street where the incident took place?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was Zmaja Od Bosna or I guess it's Mese Selimovica.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mese Selimovica, Osma Odbonna.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Osma Odbonna. It depends on the map. I think they changed the name. I'm not sure. This was 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand, this was in front of the Holiday Inn, and the street's name was Zmaja Od Bosna?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the angle street behind the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So it was not in Zmaja Od Bosna Street but some other street which exits into the Zmaja Od Bosna Street?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall exactly the streets, because it's been many years since I knew the streets there, and I never memorised all the streets.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you indicate Trebevic on the map, please, and from what part of Trebevic did the sniper shooting come from towards that street?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Trebevic is in -- Trebevic is in this area up here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We can't see your hand on the screen, so please use the ELMO in such a way that we also can follow the hand of the witness indicating where Trebevic would have been. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This area here is where Trebevic is. Here's the street that was shot at down here. And you want me to indicate exactly what?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. You said the street which was fired at. Could you clarify that? That's the street. We see the street. And at what point was the firing done from Mount Trebevic? What point on Mount Trebevic did the firing come from?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was above the area of the Jewish cemetery but up from very high angle from the lower hill, from this area here. You could see the tracers coming down every third, fourth shot was a tracer shot.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark that spot, please. May I assist you? Have you marked the spot?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I can only give you the general area, because I don't know exactly where, by this map. I would have to look at an image, a visual image. This area here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you then please mark that "D2" so that we'll ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you read out what it says in the circle, the two digits? They're not very visible. The words. I see that it says "Colina Kapa, Bistrik Kula." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Bistrik Kula. You're correct, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And does it say Colina Kapa, 966?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: It does. It says Colina Kapa, does it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you allow for the possibility that from this portion, this section, the one that says Colina Kapa and the circle you drew around this area, that the bullet came from that area?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Actually, it was higher up. It was closer to the road area. I'm going to redraw that circle, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You may. I have nothing against that.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: This will be D2 and this will be deleted.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, you have circled the Bogusavac area.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I have failed to indicate to you that we would have a break soon a couple of minutes ago and invite you to find a proper moment to stop. My apologies for that. Would this be a point to have the break or not? Otherwise the last portion would be rather short.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. I suggest that we have a short break in order to use our time as good as possible and start at 5 minutes to 12.00 -- to 1.00. I'm mistaken. We are adjourned until 5 to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Usher has left the courtroom in order to bring in Mr. Ashton, I suppose. Ms. Pilipovic, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, on the map, you indicated the location where Bogusavac can be found, together with Bistrik Kula and Colina Kappa, D1 and D2. Would you show me on the map where the cable car is.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Wait, please. The cable car is in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that Bistrik Kula is situated at the height of 1.004 metres, Bogusavac, 1.164, and Colina Kapa, 966?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot read the heights on this map. If I had a clearer map to look at, that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that those positions are situated on an altitude of approximately 1.000 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You told us that, as far as you are aware, those were the positions of the army of Republika Srpska, that is, Bistrik Kula and Vidikovac.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge as to the fact that in the vicinity of those positions were the positions of the army of BH?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only what was pointed out to me as the front line from a Serb position. I want to make note here that there was also another position where sniping came down into that same street, if I could make a circle.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I am now asking you only about this particular incident, and I would like to know whether you have any knowledge as to the fact that the positions of the BH army were in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know exactly where their line was.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Sarajevo, did you come to know at a later point in time where the positions of the BH army were and did you ever visit the positions of the BH army in that area?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I never visited the BH army, just the forces of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You're saying you never visited the BH army. Are you referring to the area that I'm now asking you about or generally speaking, that you never, ever visited the positions of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just in the area that you're speaking about now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I can therefore conclude that you did visit BH army positions in some other areas of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I shall later on go back to that question, but now let us try to clarify where exactly this area was where this incident took place. Did you see the bullets coming in, or is it that you heard the shots being fired?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: First I heard the shots being fired and then I saw the shots coming down in the form of tracers.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How far were you from that spot where this old lady and a girl were shot at?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was approximately 20 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you see the point of impact, that is, where the bullet struck?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: With respect to the place where you were, could you explain to us where those bullets hit?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were at a 45-degree angle to me. I was at the corner of the Holiday Inn, facing that angled street. The bullets came down across in front of me and hit the street and ricochetted up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What is the distance between the place, that is, the location from which the fire was opened, the area which you circled, Bogusavac, and the point at which the bullet actually struck? What is the distance between these two locations, please?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately from the area of the circles, 1.500 metres, approximately. I have no exact ...

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of sniper rifles the army of Republika Srpska had?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only those which I saw at a later time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us what sniper rifles we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a 12.7 millimetre rifle in this area up here where I've circled, and another one lower down, in another area. As far as sniper rifles, I saw other types as well, 7.62.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the range is of the sniper rifles 7.62?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Approximately 1.000 metres, depending on the rifle. If it's an assault rifle, it's less.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me if I tell you that the shooting from 7.62 is best achieved at the distance up to 400 metres?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're using an M-76 sniper rifle, you can get a lot better -- a lot more accurate than that. In the case of Republika Srpska, I saw two of those, with high-velocity scopes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: According to you, what would be the highest range of 7.62?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say a thousand metres.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what kind of sniper rifle was being used at that time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it was a larger-calibre round of the 12.7 or larger round.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How is it that you know that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because the shells were very large, the impact was much larger than a 7.62, and when they hit the wall, they did a lot of damage when they ricochetted up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So it is on the basis of that that you are concluding that the sniper rifle that was used was not 7.62?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. There was a very loud sound also associated with the rifle, much louder than a 7.62 weapon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In view of your knowledge of sniper rifles, can you tell the difference between the fire opened from a sniper rifle and an ordinary rifle?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the methodology of the shooting.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Would you explain that to us, what exactly do you mean by that, when it comes to the methodology?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: A sniper targets generally with one shot at a time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What about ordinary rifle fire?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you were using an ordinary rifle from any distance, you would fire several rounds, because if you were trying to shoot someone without proper sighting or without the proper equipment, you would have to expend several rounds possibly for you to get the person on the first round. And that wasn't always the case. Several times a day we would have one shot fired and a shot again, and occasionally there were shots fired in staccato.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If, according to you, the bullet came at an angle of 45 degrees, as you testified, in that situation, could one establish where the bullet has come from and in what way?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only if you were on the ground and looking back at the shooter. You could establish a general area of where the shooter was, but more by height. Frequently you would see bullets come down from a higher altitude on the hills above Sarajevo. Sometimes you would see them come from between buildings in the city.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you did not actually see the direction from which the bullet had come?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the direction, the area it came from. Yes, I could see that, because the trace started as soon as it came out of the hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You knew what that hill was at that time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Well, you stated that it had come from the Mount Trebevic. Later on you specified and said that it was from the location called Bogusavac. It is on the basis of which information that you were able to reach such a conclusion?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the Canadians arrived with an anti-sniper team, they pointed it out to me. I pointed them to the general direction I thought the fire had come from, because they arrived after the shooting had stopped. Then the shooting began again from that position and the Canadians knew exactly where it was, and I spoke with them after that about the position.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As far as I understand you, after the incident happened, the location was visited by Canadians. When you say "Canadians," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Canadian United Nations Protection Force, UNPROFOR. They came to the location where the bullets were hitting on the street and placed an APC in place.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How soon did they arrive?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd say within 15 minutes, 20 minutes, somewhere in that time area, time frame.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did they make any notes? Did they compile a report or take photographs of the location, or did they just talk to you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if they made an incident report or not. When their vehicle was hit, I'm sure they made an incident report of that. They would have to. It's required by their military commanders.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you do not have any specific knowledge that any incident report was eventually made of this incident and in what way the incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, ma'am.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You testified that you had come close to the old lady. Is that correct, that you went up to her?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. When she froze in the street, I went up to her.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What happened to the girl?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: She ran to the corner.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you take any pictures of the location where the incident happened?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't. It happened too fast.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you take any pictures of the spot where, according to you, the bullets hit the street?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have photographs of that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And you do have those photographs?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have those photographs. There are existing images of that intersection, that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do the photographs show the spot that the bullets hit?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Later on, did you take those photographs to the Canadians, as you call them?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only UN organisation that ever saw copies of my photograph was UNHCR. I never showed pictures to the military forces that were there under UNPROFOR.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you show any -- did you report the incident to any of the authorities, in view of the fact that you said that the Canadians made no incidence report?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I briefly mentioned it to the G4 commander sector in Sarajevo with the French battalion, yes and to UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "briefly mentioned," does that mean that you told them orally or did you write a report of any kind?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told them orally that there had been a sniping incident in that behind the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: The old woman who you say was shot at, where was she injured? What spot on her body, or what spot?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: She was in a state of shock.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that the bullets which you say came from the Bogusavac direction hit the pavement and ricochetted?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They came down and ricochetted back upwards.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: At what distance was this in comparison to the old woman and the girl? How far away were they from the spot where the bullets hit the pavement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't see the first bullet actually hit. I saw the second bullet hit right by her feet, maybe one metre past her, on the ground by her feet.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What time of day was it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When did the Canadians arrive? You said after 15 minutes, I believe.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Between 15, maybe 20 minutes later, if I recall correctly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Near the Holiday Inn, where you were staying, was there any kind of military checkpoint or military installation?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I saw, but the front lines were not too far away, over by the old congress building on the other side, by the Miljacka River, behind the museum, which is right across the street from the Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you tour the lines?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never able to go to that location. It was forbidden for anybody to go in there, any foreigners or journalists or humanitarians were not allowed in that particular area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: How do you know that the lines were there? Did you hear that or did you see it for yourself?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I met some Bosnian soldiers who had told me about their experiences there. They worked in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So we can conclude that that was where the positions of the BH army were, in that area, the soldiers of the BH army; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, about 100 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say "about a hundred metres away," referring to their positions, a hundred metres from what?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: 100 metres from the front side of the Holiday Inn, about 200 metres from where the incident occurred that we're referring to in these -- with the old woman and the girl.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: May I take it that the front line was at that point of 100 metres away?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the front of the Holiday Inn, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: What do you mean and how do you -- what is your definition of the front line? What do you mean had you say "front"?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As it was described to me and as I saw it eventually, the front line was the confrontation line dividing Republika Srpska forces and Bosnian forces. In some places it was only 25 metres apart; in other places there was maybe 100, 200, 300 metres in areas I never went to, but I heard there was some distance between some of the lines. But the Bosnians had a defensive line all the way around the city. United Nations made a map of this and plotted any changes in that front line, whether Serb advancements or Bosnian advancements or retreats.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, the front line is the line between the two warring parties, so we have two warring parties, we have the BH army, and we have the army of Republika Srpska. Those are the two parties. Now, on the map, in relation to the Holiday Inn, would you mark the positions of the BH army and the positions of the army of Republika Srpska. You say the distance was a hundred metres from Holiday Inn.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note you're working with the larger map that I was working with the other day. Can I have the larger map to point that out on?

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think the witness might mean the map that he marked, which is not larger, but a larger-scale map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I should like to ask the witness to mark the markings in this map, because we're going to use that map later on in evidence, so this would avoid a misunderstanding. Both the Prosecution and the Defence will be using that particular map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, of course both maps are there to be tendered into evidence, but if the Defence prefers to have the markings on this map. But if the witness has any difficulty in marking, then he may tell us, so that we can see whether the parties or the Chamber can assist him.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In fact, on this copy, it's already marked. The front line is there. Do you have the same copy?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't. I haven't got that copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But I should like to ask you if you could -- if we could zoom in on the screen so we can see your markings better.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. If you could come down to here, please, closer in. Where these Xes are -- stop - Xs are, here's the Holiday Inn I'm pointing to now and where these Xs are was the actual line on the Serb side on that side of the river and on the Bosnian side, on this side of the river in this line of buildings here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you mark -- can you put a line at the positions of the BH army, draw a line, please, compared to the positions that you marked for the army of Republika Srpska. You have marked in the positions of the Republika Srpska army. Would you now indicate to us and mark the BH army positions.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. If it's okay with you, I'll mark them in black Xs and I'll make that Exhibit D2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think the marking, we are at D3, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you just, let's say, use a dotted line. That will be clear enough, even without any numbering of it.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you see that dotted line?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm able to see it.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] D3, we said, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I said it was not necessary, but since you started, D3.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So taking the position from the Holiday Inn, we see that the confrontation line is here, between the two warring parties, and that it is 100 metres away from the Holiday Inn. Is that right? Do we agree on that? That is, 100 to 150 metres, as you said. The lines were about 150 metres, stretched along -- stretching along the Miljacka River. Do you agree with that description?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, keeping many mind I did not actually see that front line, but that's approximately the area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In respect to the positions, the BH army positions, behind them were residential buildings; is that right? Would you show us the -- point the Holiday Inn to us once again, please. Point the Holiday Inn out to us, please.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's the Holiday Inn. The nearest residential buildings I saw were right here, these two buildings back here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what those two buildings were?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were high apartment building, connected. There were two buildings there and these were apartment buildings back here as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, might I respectfully suggest that those buildings be marked in some way so that it becomes apparent for those who might read the transcript later which buildings were indicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so, Mr. Ashton.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: D4 were all apartment buildings, those buildings there. They were occupied by civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there were any business buildings there, and if so, could you mark them. What about the UNIS building, was that, the UNIS company building?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's over here. And these, the museum was directly across the street from the Holiday Inn, of course. Down here was the university complex. This was an office building, but I don't know what it was, and then the congress tower was here.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In this area where you pointed out the office blocks and the apartment blocks, could you tell us whether there was a barracks there, and if so, where?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The barracks is as you see right here, Tito barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you mark the barracks, please.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's marked D5, Tito barracks.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: During your stay in Sarajevo, did you happen to visit the barracks at all?

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, yes. I was taken to the barracks by the Bosnian army once, for questioning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: From your answer, we are able to conclude that the Bosnian army was located in those barracks.

utterances.speaker: JOHN ASHTON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Bosnian army was located in those barracks, and there was also an UNPROFOR contained in the barracks. The Ukranians took over the north end -- the east end was taken over by the Ukranian battalion, the Bosnians were in these couple of buildings right here. The French before also took over this area back in here, behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again I'd ask that the -- part of the Tito barracks that were occupied by the Bosnian troops be indicated on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so, Mr. Ashton.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You state that you were taken there for questioning and that you were taken there by the army of Bosnian Serbs. How long did you spend in the building when you were questioned?

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: Negative. I did not state that I was taken there by the Bosnian Serbs. I was taken by the Bosnian army. Maybe that was an incorrect -- maybe a mis --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said the Bosnian soldiers, I believe.

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: Yes. I meant the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. That's what I meant too. Perhaps I misspoke. You said, "The Bosnian soldiers took me to the barracks." Now, how long did you stay at the barracks?

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: About one hour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: May we then take it that in this part of the barracks where the Bosnian army was located, that it was the headquarters of the Bosnian army and that it was a military target? What would you say, according to you?

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: In all honesty, Ms. Pilipovic, I cannot say -- I cannot say it was a target. However, I was taken there to an office of an officer to be questioned, and I did not see any indication it was a headquarters, but I didn't see any indication it was not either.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: But I think we agree that you were questioned by an officer. Was he a military officer, an army officer?

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: Yes, ma'am. He was a uniformed Bosnian army officer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you entered the building, was security provided for the building by a service, that is to say, were there uniformed guards providing security for the building?

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: There were soldiers in the hallway when I came into the building and there was one soldier outside, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In front of the entrance to the building?

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: He was standing on the steps at the entrance of the building.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I just go back for a moment to that second half of the image, that is to say, the place you indicated. Could we move down the map a bit. Further down, where it says "Grbavica." Further down to "Grbavica." We agreed that that was where the front lines were, the confrontation line, and that the distance was 100 metres between them. You explained which buildings existed. Now, could you tell us, in this area here, which buildings existed. What were the buildings in this area here where it says "Grbavica," in the area where it says "Grbavica." Further down, where it says "Grbavica."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask for a clarification at this moment? In the translation it says that there was a hundred metres between the lines of the respective forces. I have in my mind that the witness said that the line was both sides of the river and approximately 100 metres from the Holiday Inn hotel. I don't know whether I'm mistaken or not, but could the witness just clarify this, whether there was a hundred metres between the lines or -- Mr. Ashton.

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: My knowledge was only from information provided in conversations I had with people. It was approximately 20 to 25, sometimes 30 metres in that general area along that line. That line on the Bosnian side, the Bosnian line itself was physically 100, 150 metres from the Holiday Inn. Does that clarify the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that clarifies that the summary which was contained in the question does not correspond with the answer given by you earlier. Ms. Pilipovic, would you please see whether this urges you put any other questions or to rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I asked the witness, looking at this section, where the front lines were. He explained to us what he meant by the front lines and he marked in the positions of one side and the positions of the other side. I don't think that is contested. The Xs, or crosses, as far as I was able to understand, notes the positions of the army of Republika Srpska and the other black line was the BH army positions. And the witness has just indicated and marked in the apartment blocks in that area, the residential buildings. Now my question is: What residential buildings existed around where it says "Grbavica," which means below the positions marked as the positions of the Bosnian Serb army.

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: I understand the question. Okay. To my knowledge, I didn't go into this area, but apparently to the -- this area where I am now, where I'm pointing to now, there were a few apartment buildings next to the university area here, in that area. I don't know how many civilians lived in that -- or how many people lived in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you about the area further down, where it says "Grbavica." What apartment blocks or residential buildings existed there, if there were any, and what kind? Lower down?

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: You mean over in this side of the line, is that what you're referring to, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on that side of the line, further down?

utterances.speaker: D6
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. There were several apartment buildings along here, and two-, three-storey houses in the area as well, concrete blocks.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, again that evidence will not make much sense in the transcript. Could I respectfully suggest that it at least be characterised in this way, that the witness has indicated some black rectangles which appear on the map immediately below the line of purple crosses and above the word "Grbavica," which appears printed on the map and which has a purple circle cutting through the word. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that clarifies at least what the witness has pointed out. Please, Ms. Pilipovic, as far as possible, would you please always ask the witness to mark on the map what he says, although I'm aware that we might end up with a rather complicated map at the end. This also brings me -- it's a quarter to 2.00 now --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think the witness understood my question, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was to mark in, in the section where it says "Grbavica," which buildings existed and what kind of buildings they were, if he's able to tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please do so, Mr. Ashton, and then we'll have a break, because the courtroom will be needed to be prepared for the afternoon session.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. And also, Your Honour, it would help if I had a finer-point black pen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I can imagine. If you would just do this marking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: D7 is an area which I visited, which is a residential area --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- with military activity in it. I went to those front lines. There was quite a bit of military materiel mixed in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I think we'll have to stop at this moment. I indicated to the parties that we'll not sit tomorrow. We will be in courtroom 3 --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on Wednesday and we'll start at 9.00 in the morning, and we'll adjourn until then. Would you please -- Mr. Usher, could you please get the marked original back so that it's in the hands of the registrar. As far as I'm aware, as of this moment we have still some documents that have to be tendered into evidence, and it's the black-and-white map, 3644, which will now be returned to the Registry. We'll have -- that's a "P" document. We have P3641 still to be tendered. That's a bundle of photos. We have P3645 and 3645-1, which is a premarked map. And then as far as Defence exhibits are concerned, we have D12 still to be tendered, a report of a statement given by Roy Thomas, and photos of military equipment, D13 up until D21, D21 included. So we'll stay in recess until Wednesday morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 16th day of January 2002, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.50 p.m.,
